clues.text: This man was born after Zeus disguised himself as Alcmene’s husband, Amphitryon, and he was forced to serve Omphale for three years while dressed in women’s clothing.
This figure killed his music teacher Linus after a bad lesson.
This figure defeated Thanatos in a duel in order to win back Alcestis from the dead.
After committing murder, this man was sentenced to serve as a slave to Queen Omphale for one year.
The blood of the centaur Nessus was used to poison a shirt that this man’s wife, Deianira, accidentally gave to him, ultimately killing him.
This figure's wife Deianira gave him a poisoned shirt, which led to his death and an eventual marriage to Hebe.
As a child, he strangled two snakes that were sent to kill him.
After killing his wife Megara in a fit of rage induced by Hera, this hero was sent to accomplish many tasks as penance.
Name this Greek hero and son of Zeus, who accomplished the Twelve Labors.
Name this Greek hero, an enemy of Hera, most noted for his Twelve Labors.
This figure once joined the thiasus of Dionysus after losing a drinking contest to him.

According to the Bibliotheca (“bib-lee-uh-thee-kuh”) of Pseudo-Apollodorus, this man had to pray to his father in order to defeat the brothers Bergion and Albion, which earned him the nickname of “the Kneeler.”
Amused by their jokes, this figure released the monkey-like Cercopes, who had robbed him of his weapons, and his murder of Iphitus resulted in his serving at the court of Omphale.
After throwing Iphitus (“if-i-tuhs”) off the walls of Tiryns (“tir-inz”), this man was forced to serve Omphale (“Ohm-fal-i”).
This man killed all the sons of Laomedon except Priam and completed one task with the help of his nephew Iolaus after the murder of his children with Megara.
Philoctetes lit this hero’s funeral pyre, after which he was given this hero’s bow and poison-tipped arrows.
This figure was forced to serve his cousin Eurystheus after accidentally killing his children with Megara.
This hero drove out the Stymphalian Birds, obtained the Golden Apples of the Hesperides, and slew the Nemean Lion while serving under Eurystheus.
He aided the Olympian gods during Gigantomachy and also cleaned the Augean stables.
Name this Greek hero who completed Twelve Labors, which included killing the Hydra.
Because this man once slept with the nymph Melite, Zeus forbade her from sexual relations afterwards.

The Egyptian king Busiris was killed after he tried to sacrifice this figure to the gods, and this man wrestled with and broke the horn of the river god Achelous to win the right to marry a Calydonian princess.
This figure punished two hairy weapon thieves, the Cercopes, by hanging them on a shoulder pole.
This man is cheated out of one-tenth of the cattle promised to him by a king whom he deposes and replaces with Phyleus.
Galanthis was turned into a weasel for helping in the birth of this figure.
This man married Hebe and gave his arrows to Philoctetes after dying of poison left by the centaur Nessus for Deianeira.
This hero’s weapons, which were needed by the Greeks to win the Trojan War, were given to Philoctetes.
This husband of Deianira slayed the two-headed dog Orthrus so he could steal the cattle of Geryon, and he enlisted the help of his nephew Iolaus to slay a creature in Lerna.
He kissed and killed Hippolyta for her girdle, and rerouted a river to clear the Augean stables.
Name this Greco-Roman hero who completed 12 labors.
